title: Spain Algorithmic Work Decisions Inventory
one_liner: Rejected hypothesis: the final published Royal Decree 723/2026 does not contain the algorithmic-decision disclosure obligation attributed to the pre-publication government summary.

correction.finding: The final BOE text regulates information on essential employment conditions and gives workers with existing relationships a 30-working-day request path for missing Article 3/4/5 information, but a full-text check finds no occurrence of 'algorítm'. Therefore the prior candidate's core claim that this decree creates an individual right to know algorithmic systems determining working conditions or termination is not supported by the enacted text.
correction.lesson: Council-of-Ministers summaries and press coverage are discovery signals, not sufficient evidence for a regulation-triggered commercial offer. Once the enacted text exists, Wealth Engine must reconcile the hypothesis against the operative text before promotion or build.

decision.reason: The legal trigger that made the narrow offer timely is absent from the final published decree. A generic HR/AI inventory may still have value under other law, but it requires a new evidence chain and should not inherit this candidate's validation score.
decision.reopen_only_if: A separate enacted legal obligation, buyer evidence, or repeated paid operational pain specifically supports algorithmic employment-decision inventory work.

source_policy_upgrade.rule: For regulation-triggered opportunities: proposal/announcement = signal; published operative text = validation. If publication occurs after candidate creation, revalidate the exact claimed obligation, scope, dates and transitional rules before build or promotion.
source_policy_upgrade.failure_prevented: Avoids building or selling compliance around language that changed or disappeared between announcement and enactment.
